title: Identify ringed tensor comparisons with specified adjunction mates
statement: Let $v:C\to D$ induce a geometric morphism $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ between sheaf topoi of sites small in the module universe, with $u_*$ given by precomposition with $v$ and $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $R,S$ be commutative ring sheaves on $C,D$, let $I$ be the specified algebraic inverse image of $R$-modules with coefficient ring $RI$ [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image], and let $\alpha:RI\to S$. Set $LM=S\otimes_{RI}IM$, on objects and maps, using sheafified scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $P$ be direct image with scalar restriction along the adjunct $c:R\to u_*S$, with its canonical adjunction $L\dashv P$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Assume its unit is geometric inverse-image insertion followed by scalar insertion $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. Suppose $P$ has the lax structure whose tensor maps are local pure-tensor pairings and whose unit is $c$. Then the oplax structure on $L$ obtained by this specified adjunction [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate] has tensor maps equal to the normalized canonical ringed tensor isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]. In particular they are invertible. After the inverse-image tensor identification their scalar-extension formula is $s\otimes(m\otimes n)\mapsto(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$, with inverse $(s\otimes m)\otimes(t\otimes n)\mapsto st\otimes(m\otimes n)$. The oplax unit is $S\otimes_{RI}RI\to S$, $s\otimes r\mapsto s\alpha(r)$, with inverse $s\mapsto s\otimes1$.

source.place: Tags 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules) and 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); agent identification of the specified mates.

proof.text: Write $A=RI$ and $T=S\otimes_A-$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] choose the natural normalized isomorphism $a_{M,N}:I(M\otimes_RN)\cong IM\otimes_AIN$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-extension-tensor-comparison] choose $b_{H,K}:T(H\otimes_AK)\cong TH\otimes_STK$. Define $k_{M,N}=b_{IM,IN}\circ T(a_{M,N})$. It is a natural isomorphism from $L(M\otimes_RN)$ to $LM\otimes_SLN$, since the action of $L$ on morphisms is the stipulated scalar extension of $I$. Let $q_H:H\to T(H)$ denote scalar insertion. Naturality of $q$, followed by the two cited pure-tensor normalizations, says that $k_{M,N}\circ q_{I(M\otimes_RN)}$ takes the inverse image of every generalized source pure tensor to the tensor of its two inserted inverse images. Thus $q$ and $k$ satisfy exactly the normalized comparison definition [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison].

proof.text:
Let $\Phi_{X,H}:\operatorname{Hom}_S(LX,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,PH)$ be the specified adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], and let $\eta$ be its unit. Naturality of the Hom bijection gives $\Phi(f)=P(f)\circ\eta_X$: apply naturality in the target to $f:LX\to H$ and to $\Phi(\mathrm{id}_{LX})=\eta_X$. Denote the stipulated lax tensor maps of $P$ by $p$. By [lem-sfb-adjunction-oplax-mate] the actual oplax maps are characterized by
$$\Phi(d_{M,N})=p_{LM,LN}\circ(\eta_M\otimes\eta_N),\qquad \Phi(d_0)=c.$$
This uses the specified adjunction and lax structure, so identifying these adjoints identifies their actual mates.

proof.text:
Let $\mu$ be any normalized comparison [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison], including $k$ of Step 1. For $U\in C$, $m\in M(U)$ and $n\in N(U)$, apply its generalized normalization with $Z=|M|\times|N|$, the projections $x,y$, and the pure pairing $z$. Naturality of the geometric adjunction unit gives $u_*u^{-1}(z)\eta_Z=\eta_{|M\otimes_RN|}z$; naturality for the two projections identifies the two components of $\eta_Z$ with $\eta_{|M|},\eta_{|N|}$. The algebraic inverse-image identifications [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image] and the assumed formula for the module unit therefore give, on the sections over $v(U)$,
$$\mu\bigl(\eta_{M\otimes_RN}(m\otimes n)\bigr)=\eta_M(m)\otimes\eta_N(n).$$
The right side is exactly $p_{LM,LN}(\eta_M(m)\otimes\eta_N(n))$, interpreted as a section of the direct image, by the stipulated local pairing. Hence $P(\mu)\eta_{M\otimes_RN}$ and $p_{LM,LN}(\eta_M\otimes\eta_N)$ agree after the pure pairing on every object of $C$. The sheaf tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] makes them equal as $R$-linear maps; it does not require every tensor section to be globally pure. Injectivity of the bijection in Step 2 gives $\mu=d_{M,N}$. In particular $d=k$, is invertible, and equals every normalized canonical comparison.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, Hom/bilinear chain; agent identification by units and injectivity

proof.text:
After identifying $I(M\otimes_RN)$ with $IM\otimes_AIN$ using Step 1, the map $d=k$ is $b_{IM,IN}$. Put $H=IM$, $K=IN$. Its normalization and $S$-linearity give
$$b\bigl(s\otimes(m\otimes n)\bigr)=(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n).$$
Indeed multiply its insertion formula by $s$. Define the reverse pairing before sheafification by $((s\otimes m),(t\otimes n))\mapsto st\otimes(m\otimes n)$. It is additive in all four entries. The $A$-relations in the first input hold because $s\alpha(a)t\otimes(m\otimes n)=st\otimes(am\otimes n)$, and those in the second because $st\alpha(a)\otimes(m\otimes n)=st\otimes(m\otimes an)$. The $S$-balancing relation is $(rs)t=s(rt)$; commutativity of $S$ makes both input actions compatible. These formulas commute with restrictions. Extend this presheaf pairing to the two scalar-extension sheaves by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension], then to their tensor by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. The two composites on generators are $s\otimes(m\otimes n)$ and $(st\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)=(s\otimes m)\otimes(t\otimes n)$. Additivity, the same two uniqueness properties, and the sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] prove the inverse identities on the sheaves. This proves both scalar formulas, with no flatness assumption.

source.place: Section 03EK, scalar-extension equality, and Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor; agent balancing and inverse calculations

proof.text: For the tensor unit, the algebraic inverse-image identifications identify $I(R)$ with the regular $A$-module: transport of multiplication is exactly its scalar action [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. Thus $L(R)=S\otimes_AA$. Multiplication $h(s\otimes a)=s\alpha(a)$ is balanced, since $s\alpha(r)\alpha(a)=s\alpha(ra)$, and commutes with restrictions; it therefore defines a morphism of $S$-module sheaves by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Its adjoint under Step 2 is $P(h)\eta_R$. On $r\in R(U)$ this is $\alpha(\eta^{\rm geom}_R(r))=c_U(r)$, by the assumed insertion formula and the definition of $c$ as the geometric adjunct of $\alpha$. Hence $\Phi(h)=c=\Phi(d_0)$, and $h=d_0$. The map $j(s)=s\otimes1$ is $S$-linear and commutes with restrictions. On sections $hj(s)=s$, and on presheaf tensors $jh(s\otimes a)=s\alpha(a)\otimes1=s\otimes a$ by balancing. The sheafification uniqueness property gives $jh=\mathrm{id}$ on all sections. Thus $j$ is the asserted inverse of the oplax unit, also for the zero ring.
